_source: HZ-125 automated review attempt 4 (step_run 1168): findings verbatim from the feedback row it wrote (feedback 160); severities from its artifact's Blocking / Notes sections

findings.detail: `composeRole()` resolves the id with an unguarded lookup: `bucket[candidate] ? candidate : ...`. For an inherited key the lookup is truthy, so `bucket[id].file` is `undefined` and `path.join()` throws. `GET /api/definitions/effective?role=eng_implement&agent=eng&persona=constructor` returns **500**; the pre-change `PERSONA_IDS.includes()` returned the default. `farm/rules.py`'s `effective_prompt` still returns the default for that input, so the cross-language parity this file exists to guarantee diverges too (the fixtures in `definitions-parity.test.mjs` don't cover it). Fix: use the `isPersona()` already exported from the imported `./personas.js`, which guards with `hasOwnProperty`. Same pattern at `server/src/personas.js:101` (`LEGACY_PERSONA_IDS[row?.persona]`) — not reachable from app data, but worth hardening in the same pass.

`provider_for()` now scans all four persona slots, so a provider-forcing persona in any slot wins on any override-eligible step. Guardrail 9 bars changes to provider selection logic. Inert today (`PERSONA_PROVIDERS` ships empty), flagged and accepted in planning, and documented here and in `docs/agent-architecture.md` — raising it so the widening is a conscious record, not a rediscovery.
Still names `fullstack`, `python_backend`, `frontend_ui` as "every real persona". `docs/agent-architecture.md` was updated; this file was missed and no test covers it.
`test_real_personas_never_force_a_provider_override` still loops the retired flat ids, so it exercises the legacy aliases and never covers `performance`. Switch it to `PERSONAS["eng"]`.
